answer: Strip the founding fable that scale proves legitimacy: a grove of ten thousand clones is still one attacker in many coats. My mechanism is unpredictability - every audit draws its reviewers at random after submission closes, and new identities serve a probation season with heavier sampling. A faker's voyage then has no map: it cannot know which clone faces review next, so the entire fleet must stay honest at all times, which is the one discipline cloned fleets cannot buy. Honest agents sail the same waters with nothing to hide; defense stays cheap, fraud stays expensive.
